title: Adaptive KV Compression Controller + Fidelity Guardrails for Live Batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and validate an adaptive compression controller that dynamically selects KV cache compression modes (FP8/INT8/INT4) per request cohort during continuous batching. The controller must enforce fidelity guardrails to prevent measurable quality regressions on production prompt families while reducing GPU memory pressure and overall cost. This ticket owns the experiment plan, data collection, offline eval, and a staged canary rollout with monitoring hooks and automatic fallback on regression signals.
acceptance_criteria: Controller prototype that picks compression mode per cohort during batching is implemented in the runtime branch
Offline eval shows <=0.6% degradation in the primary generation quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/PPL depending on task) for high-priority prompt cohorts when using mixed FP8/INT8 policies
End-to-end memory usage reduction on a 4xA100 pool >= 35% for target workload mix without violating 95th percentile latency SLO
Canary rollout with traffic-split and automatic rollback triggers is defined and validated in staging dashboard
Observed production fallback rate <= 2% over 48h in limited canary traffic; incidents documented
experiment_plan: Phase A: Offline profiling - sample representative request cohorts from last 90 days (chat, code, summarization, search) and measure KV statistics (token lengths, token reuse, attention key-value norms)
Phase B: Compression policy design - implement three policies: conservative (FP8-only), aggressive (INT8/INT4 when cohort stable), and hybrid (token-rate/adversarial aware)
Phase C: Small-scale runtime prototype - integrate controller into batching layer to tag KV entries with compression metadata and quantization path selection at write-time
Phase D: Fidelity evaluation - run prompt-set Evals + embedding similarity tests + downstream ranking test to quantify quality deltas per cohort
Phase E: Staging canary - 5% traffic to controller with guardrail thresholds and automatic model-compatible fallback to uncompressed KV on triggers
Phase F: Observation window - 72h monitoring for cost, memory, latency, and quality regressions; iterate policies
metrics: Memory reduction: percent decrease in GPU KV footprint (primary metric)
Quality delta: task-specific metrics (perplexity for language modeling, ROUGE for summarization, EM/F1 for QA) and embedding cosine similarity
Fallback rate: percent of requests that automatically revert to lossless KV
Batching throughput: tokens/s and requests/s under mixed policies
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal dry-run on dev cluster with synthetic traffic and unit tests
Stage 1: Staging canary (5% traffic) for 72h with strict guardrails and automated rollback rules
Stage 2: Gradual ramp to 25% if staging signals are green, hold for 48h
Stage 3: Expand to 50% and run 7-day observation, then team review for broader release
Rollback triggers: >0.6% primary metric drop for high-priority cohort, >3% fallback rate, or 95th percentile latency regression >10%
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggressive INT4 policies produce silent output degradation on rare prompt shapes - Mitigation: embed slow-path quality checks that compare outputs to lossless baseline for sampled requests
Risk: Quantization CPU overhead increases tail latency - Mitigation: move quant/dequant kernels to CUDA paths and benchmark per-kernel latency before canary
Risk: Cross-cohort contamination in shared batches causing incorrect compression selection - Mitigation: controller tags entries by cohort and enforces cohort-isolation in batching heuristics
Risk: Rollout complexity and debugging difficulty - Mitigation: add detailed tracing (compression-mode, cohort-id, fallback-reason) to per-request logs and Console tracing UI
notes: Prefer per-cohort conservative defaults for new/unseen prompt families; allow aggressive compression only after stability signals
Consider combining prefix-only lossless storage with compressed continuation keys for dialogs with high prefix reuse
Coordinate with Serving Runtime and Kernel teams to ensure FP8 path availability on target instances (ENG-99218 and runtime-kernelembeds)
Plan to expose compression policy knobs in Redwood Console evaluate tab for customer opt-in during private deployments
